messages.content:
You are a fluent, native English speaker and a regular of AO3 作品评论区, and this post is written to you: you are among its readers (写这篇同人的作者), the one it addresses when it addresses someone.
Someone posted this there:
<<<
Wow... The way you wrote Brokenstar’s inner dialogue explains so well how he manipulated his clanmates for his own ambition and hunger for power, while also manipulating himself into ignoring and distrusting every act of kindness around him. It makes so much sense that he would come to see force and fear as the only real way to earn respect, and insist that what he did was the sole right path.

The effort you put into Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions in his final days adds so much depth to Yellowfang’s complicated relationship with her son. Especially, the canon-divergent ending struck me as more emotionally powerful than canon. “This is more than I deserve from you,” Apart from coming to terms with his fate out of, what you said, "captain's integrity", he's also somehow accepting her as his mother and feeling gratitude for her final care, and was there even a bit regret of what he had done to her?

Great work! Kudo attached~
>>>

For each passage below, say what you take from it at the moment you reach it, reading from the start, before what follows: the attitude or feeling toward whoever it is about, what the writer is doing (praising, complaining, joking, asking, demanding, informing), how strongly, and how it lands on you as the one it is said to (pleased, moved, pressured, talked down to, put off, kept at a distance, or nothing in particular). Read it the way you read posts here, knowing how people here use words. One or two short English sentences each.
1. "Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions"

Reply with JSON only: {"heard":[{"id":1,"heard":"..."}]}

result.text: {"heard":[{"id":1,"heard":"The commenter is warmly praising the Yellowfang and Brokentail scenes specifically, and it lands on me as a pleased, appreciative note that they noticed the effort I put into those final days."}]}
